note: Original classroom practice. Independent academic review pending.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Explain how a mould can reproduce a shape across clay pieces.
questions.prompt: A group is preparing several clay tokens with the same raised design. Its teacher supplies a reusable press mould with a recessed design. Explain why the design comes out raised on a token and why using the same mould helps the tokens match.
questions.answer: Soft clay fills the recessed part of the mould. When released, the clay that filled that recess projects above the surface. Using the same mould transfers the same design to each token.
questions.explanation: A recess in the mould provides space for a raised feature on the clay piece.

markingGuide.description: Explains that clay fills the recessed area.
Explains that the clay from the recess becomes a projection after release.
Links repeatability to using the same mould.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Choose modelling tools for a stated surface and thickness problem.
questions.prompt: A pupil is making a flat clay plaque. The surface is lumpy and one corner is thicker than the others. Which plan addresses both issues before the plaque dries?
questions.answer: Use a smooth roller with equal-height guide strips, then check the edges.
questions.explanation: The roller levels the surface and the paired guides keep the rolling height even across the clay.
options: Press the thick corner with a pointed tool to add a pattern.
Measure only the length of the plaque with a ruler.
Use a smooth roller with equal-height guide strips, then check the edges.
Turn the plaque on a banding wheel without reshaping it.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.subtopic: Focus and contrast in a group
questions.learningObjective: Explain how contrasting movement can direct an audience’s attention.
questions.prompt: A group dance needs the audience to notice a brief action by one dancer. The teacher suggests the other dancers hold still during that action, then move again. Explain how this plan creates contrast and directs attention.
questions.answer: The group’s stillness contrasts with the solo dancer’s movement, so the solo action stands out. When the group resumes, attention can return to the ensemble.
questions.explanation: A change in who is moving can create a clear focal point without moving the soloist to the front.

markingGuide.description: Identifies the contrast between stillness and movement.
Explains how the contrast draws attention to the solo action.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Create and perform a movement motif passed between dancers with a variation.
questions.prompt: In a supervised trio, devise a two-action motif. Dancer A performs it, dancer B repeats both actions, then dancer C performs both actions with one clear change of level or direction. Use marked spaces and demonstrate the sequence twice. A seated version is acceptable.
questions.answer: For example, A and B each reach forward and sweep sideways in turn. C makes the reach low and keeps the sweep. The trio repeats that order on the second run.
questions.explanation: Keeping the actions recognisable lets the audience see the motif pass between dancers and notice the planned variation.

markingGuide.description: Passes the motif from A to B with both actions intact.
Makes a clear variation of level or direction in C’s turn.
Repeats the sequence in order with clear handoffs.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Explain how evidence of recognition and influence can support describing a musician as an icon.
questions.prompt: A class display profiles a fictional Nigerian musician. One note says audiences in several towns recognise the musician’s work. Another says younger musicians cite that work as an influence. Explain how these details support describing the musician as an icon.
questions.answer: Recognition in several places suggests a reputation beyond one audience. References by younger musicians suggest the work has influenced other artists. Together these provide grounds for describing the musician as an icon.
questions.explanation: An icon is widely recognised and can have a lasting influence in a field. The description should be supported by evidence of reputation or influence.

markingGuide.description: Links recognition in several towns to a wider reputation.
Links references by younger musicians to influence.
Uses the evidence to explain the description as an icon.
